text: Tata Motors Q2 FY27 consolidated profit rebounded to ₹1,257 crore and revenue increased 36.3%.
The Indian passenger‑vehicle market expanded 28.3% YoY to around 26.4 lakh units during April‑Sept FY27.
JM Financial forecasts TMCV’s revenue to rise 43.6% YoY to Rs 24,218.4 crore in Q2 FY27.
If shareholders approve a restructuring proposal, the required acceptance threshold could be lowered from 95% to 80%, improving the chance of closing the acquisition.

Three Iveco investors holding roughly 20.4 % of shares could realise a combined gain of about €63 million at the €14.40 offer price, making their participation critical for reaching the 80 % threshold.

Analysts preview Tata Motors CV Q2 FY27, expecting revenue to rise 44‑45 % YoY and volume growth of about 43 % YoY, driven by LCVs (+53.1 %). Profit after tax forecasts diverge (44.3 % vs 25.7 % growth) and margins may be pressured by input‑cost inflation.
Tata Motors raised its all‑cash takeover offer for Iveco to €14.40 per share, valuing the transaction at €3.91 billion.

Iveco shareholders endorsed Tata Motors’ bid, cutting the acceptance threshold to 80 per cent and confirming the raised offer price of EUR 14.40 per share, valuing the transaction at around EUR 3.8 billion. The approval enables amendments for delisting, board appointments and termination of the loyalty voting structure, with the tender period running from September 7 to October 26, 2026.
note: Shareholders approved the resolutions but did not confirm the price (Tata raised it earlier); €3.8 billion is the 2025 deal value, not the value at €14.40.

text: Post‑acquisition, the combined business would generate annual revenue of about €21 billion and sell over 590,000 vehicles.
The acquisition offer was increased to €14.40 per share from €14.10.

Analysts preview Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles (TMCV) Q2 FY27 results, expecting profit growth up to 44% YoY and revenue up 44‑45% YoY, driven by roughly 43% YoY volume expansion. Margin pressure and pricing actions are highlighted as key factors.
India is increasingly being positioned as a hub for developing and exporting vehicles, as evidenced by Stellantis’ expanded partnership with Tata Motors to build cars for over 50 markets.
Tata Motors needs to secure 80% shareholder acceptance for its €3.9 billion acquisition of Iveco, with silent shareholders holding the decisive votes.
The combined Tata‑Iveco business is projected to generate annual revenue of about €21 billion and sell over 590,000 vehicles.
Analysts expect Tata Motors CV Q2 FY27 revenue to rise about 44‑45 % YoY, with estimates ranging from Rs 24,218.4 crore to Rs 24,638.1 crore, driven by volume growth of about 43 % YoY.
The offer price for Iveco was increased by 2 % to €14.40 per share.
As of 21 Oct, shareholders had tendered about 33.4% of Iveco’s shares; the offer closes on 26 Oct, leaving three trading days to achieve the 80% threshold.
